This report consolidates medical assessments conducted between 10:00 AM and 1:30 PM on Friday, 17 May 2024, following the conclusion of the final pre-match training session. All players listed below have undergone standard orthopedic screening, cardiac baseline checks, and neuromuscular function evaluations as per league-mandated protocols. Temperature and pitch conditions at the time of assessment were recorded at 11.3°C and firm, respectively, with no anticipated weather disruptions affecting player status prior to kick-off.

**City United FC – Player Availability Status**

*Questionable (Game-Time Decision)*
- #7, Midfielder – Left hamstring tightness (Grade 1 strain, sustained during training on 15 May). Participated in modified warm-up and closed-session drills. Final determination pending post-activation mobility metrics and GPS load data from morning re-test. Medical staff reports no swelling or bruising; player remains on anti-inflammatory protocol with compression garment use.
- #14, Defender – Right ankle instability (non-traumatic, recurrent). Completed 45 minutes of positional work under supervision. Subjective feedback indicates intermittent discomfort during lateral pivoting; decision to be made following team captaincy consultation and kit-fitting simulation at 11:00 AM on matchday.
- #22, Forward – Mild gastroenteritis (non-contagious, isolated case). Rehydrated via IV protocol on 16 May evening. Cleared strength benchmarks but undergoing nutritional tolerance monitoring. Listed as questionable due to precautionary fatigue risk.

*Out (Unavailable)*
- None

All other members of the 25-player registered squad are confirmed fit and available for selection. Goalkeeper rotation remains unaffected, with #1 and #13 both completing full-contact drills without restriction. #3, long-term ACL recovery (injured 3 January 2024), remains in Phase 4 rehab and is not yet cleared for contact. His status is unchanged and not relevant to this match window.

**Riverside Athletic – Player Availability Status**

*Questionable (Game-Time Decision)*
- #9, Forward – Lower back stiffness (mechanical, non-disc related). Received targeted physiotherapy and dry needling on 16 May. Participated in light jogging but excluded from set-piece rehearsal. Medical team monitoring paraspinal muscle symmetry via real-time EMG.

Pre-Match Status Update – Sporting Kansas City vs. Real Salt Lake
Date of Report: May 8, 2026 | Kickoff: 7:30 PM CT | Venue: Children’s Mercy Park, Kansas City, KS
Weather Forecast: 68°F, partly cloudy, 12 mph winds from the south-southeast
Surface:天然草皮 (Bermuda Hybrid)

Medical & Performance Staff Notes:
All player statuses were confirmed following the morning recovery session and medical re-evaluation conducted at the Compass Minerals National Performance Center. The sports science team has completed GPS load monitoring from the previous match and training microcycle. Hydration indices, CRP markers, and creatine kinase levels have been reviewed for all players participating in reduced-load protocols. No infectious illness cases have been reported in the squad over the past 72 hours. Travel and sleep logs for away fixtures remain within acceptable variance.

Sporting Kansas City – Injury & Availability Status

Questionable (27% chance of playing – medical staff assessment)
- D Steffen Yeater: Right ankle sprain, sustained during 78th minute of #SKCvCLB (April 26). Completed pool-based mobility drills on May 5. Advanced to straight-line jogging on May 6. Underwent proprioception testing on May 7; slight deficit in right ankle dorsiflexion noted. Participated in 30-minute modified training on May 8. Final decision pending post-warmup assessment.
- M Cammy Brown: Left hamstring tightness, reported after training session on April 30. Initial MRI showed no tear, grade 0 strain. Currently on individualized activation program: 2x daily neuromuscular activation, eccentric loading, and gait re-education. Completed 45-minute on-field session May 7, including positional movement patterns. Team physio reports ‘positive trajectory’ but recommends caution due to recurrence risk in prior history (2025 season).
- F Daniel Salazar: Right knee contusion, incidental collision during set-piece drill on May 3. No structural damage per ultrasound. Pain-limited in sprint mechanics. Treatment: pulsed ultrasound, compression, and cryotherapy. Expected to train fully on May 9 morning.

Out (0% availability)
- D Kaveh Rezaei: Left MCL sprain, Grade II, sustained in 23rd minute of #SKCvCOL (March 21). Completed Phase III rehab: closed kinetic chain strengthening, balance integration. Currently in Phase IV: sport-specific agility. Not cleared for contact drills. Targeted return window: May 16–18.
- M Jalen Patel: Right adductor strain, Grade I, diagnosed May 1 following post-match screening. MRI confirmed minor fiber disruption. On reduced field participation. Daily manual therapy, pelvic stabilization exercises, and isometric loading progression. Expected back in training May 10.
- F Elias Nguyen: Left ankle syndesmosis irritation, persistent despite conservative care. Diagnosed April 10. Has undergone three PRP injections. Limited to non-weight-bearing cycling. No timeline for return; ongoing imaging review scheduled for May 12.

Real Salt Lake – Injury & Availability Status

Questionable (30% chance of playing)
- D Noah Trujillo: Right knee medial joint line tenderness, mechanism unclear. First reported May 2. MRI revealed mild meniscal irritation without tear. Not participated in full sessions since. Light bike work and isometrics only. Team ortho consult scheduled for May 10.
- M Dev Shah: Left ankle instability, history of inversion sprain (2024). Recurrent discomfort during lateral movements. Undergoing bracing protocol and proprioception circuit. Took part in controlled passing drills May 7 but excluded from transition work.

Out (0% availability)
- F Marcus Bell: Right ACL reconstruction, post-surgical week 24. Continuing strength symmetry work. Not cleared for cutting motions. Expected return: July 2026.
- D Eliot Frost: Left shoulder dislocation, non-contact injury during training (April 18). Surgical fixation performed April 20. Immobilized phase complete. Now in early active ROM. No return before June.
- M Rico Mendez: Right knee patellar tendinopathy, chronic. Removed from rotation since April 12. Currently in load-modification program with cross-training. No on-field participation.

Additional Notes:
Both teams have submitted travel rosters compliant with MLS roster rules. Sporting KC’s medical staff has coordinated pitch condition assessment with grounds crew; recent moisture levels are within optimal range. No environmental risk factors expected. All listed injuries are medically documented via electronic health record (EHR) entries from team physicians. No disciplinary suspensions or non-injury-related absences are present in either squad.

Reporting Officer: Medical & Performance Department, Manchester United

This report outlines the current status of players within the first-team squad ahead of the upcoming fixture against Brentford. This group includes midfielders Scott McTominay, Bruno Fernandes, and Mason Mount; defenders Luke Shaw, Diogo Dalot, and Raphaël Varane; and forwards Alejandro Garnacho, Anthony Martial, and new signing Amad Diallo, who has now fully acclimated to the squad’s training load following his return from international duty with Guinea.

Out (5):
- Lisandro Martínez (Defender): Sustained a lower-body issue during the previous fixture against Newcastle United. Currently undergoing structured rehabilitation. No timeline for return; not participating in team training.
- Tyrell Malacia (Defender): Experiencing ongoing discomfort in the lower extremity. Progressing through individualized rehab program; no return to group sessions yet.
- Jonny Evans (Defender): Managing a lower-body muscular strain. Progressing slowly; expected to remain out for at least two additional weeks.
- Tom Heaton (Goalkeeper): Recovering from a lower-body setback. Participating in non-contact drills but not match-fit.
- Jadon Sancho (Midfielder/Winger): Not injured. Currently not included in the matchday squad due to non-medical, internal team selection considerations. Continues to train separately with the under-21s as part of a performance pathway reintegration plan.

Additional Notes:
- All players in the 'Out' category have been logged in the club’s internal medical database (MediTrack Pro v4.3) with corresponding rehabilitation timelines and biometric benchmarks.
- The sports science team has confirmed that training volumes for available players were adjusted by 15% over the weekend to optimize freshness.
- Weather conditions at Old Trafford are currently dry with a temperature of 13°C; pitch inspection conducted Sunday evening confirmed optimal playing surface.
- No dietary or sleep-cycle irregularities reported across the squad in the past 72 hours.

Final team selection will be communicated via the Premier League’s official submission portal no later than 11:00 BST. Until then, all availability statuses remain subject to final medical clearance. The club emphasizes that injury-related terminology is used generically to protect player privacy and align with internal communication protocols.

Despite five players listed as Out, none of the unavailable players are first-choice starters in the current tactical setup, and the goalkeeper position remains fully covered by on-site healthy alternatives.

state.file: 1987 Spring Exhibitions Brochure Drafts and Supplementary Materials
state.item: Handwritten Notes on Layout for Brochure Page 4
state.provenance: Originally held in the Office of the Chief Curator, Exhibitions Division; transferred following administrative review of inactive records
state.physical_description: One folded sheet of cream-colored bond paper, 21.5 x 28 cm, containing handwritten annotations in blue ballpoint ink and graphite pencil. Margins show light smudging. Paper exhibits slight yellowing along edges consistent with age. No staple or fastener present. Reverse side contains partial coffee stain, approximately 2.5 cm in diameter, located in lower right quadrant.
state.creator: Unknown staff member, Exhibitions Department
state.title: Layout Notes for 'Art in the Provincial Landscape' Brochure – Page 4 Draft
state.scope_and_content: This file contains preparatory documentation related to the design and layout of a brochure for the 1987 spring exhibition series. The primary document is a folded paper sheet bearing handwritten notes, margin annotations, and placement suggestions for text blocks and image placeholders. Includes directional arrows, size notations (e.g., 'reduce photo 10%'), and a checklist titled 'Final Review Items' with several items unchecked. No final brochure version is present in this file. Accompanying materials include a sticky note with a phone number (redacted) and a clipped newspaper clipping about a public lecture series, unrelated to the brochure content. The file folder also contains a blank photocopy sheet and a misfiled inventory tag for a ceramic vase (object ID: CER-1979-011), likely inserted in error during transfer.
state.administrative_history: The Publications and Printed Matter Collection was established in 1973 to preserve ephemeral output produced by the museum’s public programming divisions. Materials are accessioned annually following departmental audits. Files are retained for 25 years before review for deaccession or permanent preservation.
state.arrangement: Chronological by exhibition season, then by document type. This file follows 'Final Brochures' and precedes 'Correspondence with Printer'.
state.use_restrictions: Permission required for publication; credit must be given to the Provincial Heritage and Cultural Repository

descriptive_fields.title: City of Westbridge Municipal Archives Collection, General Administrative Records (1890–1975)

creator.name: City of Westbridge, Office of the Municipal Clerk

descriptive_fields.materials: Paper, cellulose acetate microfilm (positive), ballpoint and fountain ink, typewritten carbon copies, graphite annotations

dimensions.note: Variable depending on paper compression; average measured depth

measurements.format: loose sheets, bound volumes, microfilm reels (16mm), envelopes, file folders

descriptive_fields.description: This fonds comprises the accumulated administrative records of the City of Westbridge’s municipal government from 1890 to 1975. Materials include council minutes, departmental correspondence, public works reports, health inspection logs, property assessment rolls, and by-law amendments. The records were transferred to the Westbridge Regional Archives in 1977 under Deed of Gift #DG-1977-088, following municipal retention schedule MRS-4B. Files are organized according to the original departmental classification system, with minor rehousing undertaken in 1993 to replace acidic folders. The collection includes 37 microfilm reels produced between 1968 and 1974 for disaster recovery purposes; these are duplicates of original paper records held within the same fonds. Some documents exhibit water staining (primarily Boxes 22, 45, and 89) due to a basement leak in the old city hall in 1952. Minor insect activity (silverfish residue) noted in Box 112 during 2005 inspection; area treated and monitored. The majority of textual materials are in fair to good condition, with legible handwriting and stable paper. No classified or access-restricted content was identified during initial appraisal, and all records are open for research under the Municipal Freedom of Information and Protection of Privacy Act (MFIPPA). The finding aid was updated in 2010 and is available online through the Westbridge Archives Public Catalog. This collection is frequently consulted for genealogical research, property history, and urban development studies. It forms part of the larger Westbridge Community Heritage Documentation Project (WCHDP), which includes oral histories, maps, and photographs held in adjacent collections.
descriptive_fields.provenance: Transferred from the City of Westbridge Clerk's Office, 1977.

state.brief_description: A collection of seven irregularly shaped metal and wood elements, stored in a sealed polyethylene bag, received as part of a bulk donation from an estate in Westchester County. state.place_of_origin: Toronto, Ontario, Canada (reproduction); original design attributed to Hamilton, Ontario, Canada
state.materials: Steel with porcelain enamel coating, printed measurement indicators in black enamel paint

dimensions.cup_1: height: 6.2 cm, diameter: 8.5 cm, capacity: 250 mL (1 cup)
dimensions.cup_2: height: 5.8 cm, diameter: 7.7 cm, capacity: 180 mL (3/4 cup)

state.description: Set of five nesting measuring cups, graduated in metric and imperial units. Cups are white with blue decorative trim along the rim and black measurement labels on the outer surface. Handles are loop-style, formed from the same steel sheet, attached at the rim. Base of each cup is stamped with a faint 'H&H Repro 1985' mark. Set lacks original packaging but includes a folded instruction sheet in English and French, printed on low-weight paper with a caution about thermal shock and chipping. The design closely mimics a series produced by the Dominion Kitchenware Co. in the late 1920s, though minor dimensional variations and font style in the labeling indicate modern manufacturing techniques. This set was acquired as part of a teaching collection for domestic science history programs and was used in museum-led workshops between 1987 and 2003.
state.provenance: Purchased from Hearth & Home Reproductions Ltd. via mail order catalog #42B, invoice #MCT-88472, dated March 14, 1986. Originally accessioned into the Education Department’s handling kit collection.
state.cataloguing_notes: Item assessed during rehousing of Education Department kits. Original accession file includes correspondence with manufacturer confirming non-original status. No known copyright restrictions on design. Meant for handling; not part of fine collection.
state.condition: Good. Minor surface scratching consistent with classroom use. One cup (1/4 cup) has a 1.2 cm chip on the rim edge, exposing underlying steel. No structural damage. Enamel remains intact; no flaking observed under 10x magnification. Instruction sheet shows creasing and minor toning but remains legible.
state.conservation_history: None. Light cleaning performed in 2003 with damp cloth and mild detergent.
state.storage_location: Education Collection, Handling Kit Storage Unit 7B
related_collections: MA-1928-HX-0447-01 (Photograph of original 1928 Dominion Kitchenware set)
state.image_details: No photographic documentation currently attached; visual inspection conducted during cataloguing. Recommended for future imaging due to frequent use in outreach.
state.handling_instructions: May be handled in supervised educational settings. Avoid immersion in water. Use cotton gloves if handling during display setup.

state.physical_description: Bundle of 12 unbound paper sheets, mixed handwriting styles, some water damage and ink corrosion observed. Materials include laid paper, iron gall ink, and traces of sealing wax on one fragment.
state.provenance: Acquired in 1903 from a private donation in Cumbria; provenance prior to that uncertain. No direct documentation links to William or Dorothy Wordsworth, though stylistic parallels exist.
state.descriptive_notes: Contains drafts of reflective verse, nature observations, and a short diary-like entry referencing 'Grasmere light in November'. state.cataloguer_comments: Potential literary significance; may represent peripheral material from the broader Romantic literary network. Recommended for interdisciplinary review, though primary classification under historical memorabilia is appropriate due to lack of verified authorship.

state.collection_name: New York City Municipal Archives, Department of Public Works, Bureau of Bridges and Tunnels Annual Reports Collection
state.collection_title: Annual Reports and Administrative Correspondence of the Bureau of Bridges and Tunnels, 1935–1968
state.collection_extent: Approximately 42 cubic feet (108 archival boxes, 3 oversize folders)
state.collection_acquisition_method: Transferred from the Bureau of Bridges and Tunnels in accordance with city records retention schedules
state.collection_arrangement: Arranged in original order as received from the creating agency, with minor rehousing for preservation. Organized by year, then by report type (annual reports, correspondence logs, structural inspection summaries, personnel rosters, budget ledgers).
state.collection_scope_and_content: The collection consists of administrative records generated by the Bureau of Bridges and Tunnels, a division of the New York City Department of Public Works, from 1935 through 1968. Materials include annual reports to the Commissioner of Public Works, internal memoranda, correspondence with contractors and engineering firms, bridge maintenance logs, photographic documentation logs (though photographs themselves were often stored separately), personnel evaluations, and budgetary records. The records reflect the operational history of major infrastructure projects, including maintenance of the Brooklyn, Manhattan, and Williamsburg Bridges, as well as the Queens-Midtown and Brooklyn-Battery Tunnels. The documentation includes technical summaries of structural inspections, notes on material usage (e.g., steel fatigue assessments, concrete reinforcement), and correspondence regarding labor union negotiations and procurement contracts. Some files contain carbon copies of outgoing letters, handwritten annotations, and stamped routing slips. The bulk of the material is textual, with standardized report formats used from the late 1940s onward. The collection is particularly strong in documentation from the postwar period (1946–1955), reflecting increased investment in infrastructure maintenance and expansion. A small number of oversized engineering schematics and site plans were transferred with the collection and are stored in flat archival cases. The records were originally maintained in departmental filing cabinets and were accessioned as a complete set following departmental reorganization in 1971.
state.collection_abstract: Comprehensive administrative and operational records of the NYC Bureau of Bridges and Tunnels, covering engineering assessments, personnel matters, fiscal planning, and inter-agency communications over a 33-year period.
state.collection_access_conditions: Open to researchers by appointment. Some personnel files restricted for 75 years under civil service confidentiality regulations.
state.collection_use_conditions: Materials may be used for research, publication, and educational purposes with proper attribution. Requests for commercial reproduction require written permission.
collection_related_materials: NYCMA-ENG-1902-ACC-00114: Department of Public Works Engineering Division Records
NYCMA-PHOTO-1940S-BT: Photographic Collection of NYC Bridges and Tunnels Construction Projects
state.collection_appraisal_and_selection: No materials were deaccessioned. All records were retained as part of the city’s permanent archival holdings due to administrative and historical significance.
state.collection_processing_history: Processed by archival staff between 1972 and 1974. Original folder titles retained. Rehoused in acid-free boxes and folders. Finding aid created in 1975 and updated in digital format in 2003.
state.reproduction_status: Original archival records. No reproductions or facsimiles included in this collection.
state.condition: Overall good for age. Some documents show minor foxing, edge tearing, or staple rust. Carbon paper remains intact in many multi-part forms. No active mold or insect damage observed. Stabilized through standard archival housing.

state.creator: William Wordsworth, Dorothy Wordsworth
state.materials: Handwritten ink on laid paper, parchment binding
state.description: This notebook contains surviving draft fragments of William Wordsworth’s philosophical poem 'The Prelude,' composed during his residence in Grasmere. state.reproduction_status: No digital image available; reproduction restricted pending conservation review.
state.handling_notes: Sensitive to light and humidity; access limited to researchers with prior approval due to cultural significance and physical fragility.

descriptive_fields.brief_description: A single, irregularly shaped assemblage measuring approximately 28.5 cm in maximum dimension, composed of heterogeneous materials including fibrous organic matter, corroded metallic fragments, and indeterminate dark particulate matter adhered to a central rigid core. Surface texture varies from granular to flaking in areas. No inscriptions, maker's marks, or serial numbers visible under standard lighting. Weight recorded as 312 grams at time of intake. General appearance suggests possible deterioration or partial decomposition. Object was received disassembled in three loose components placed within a sealed polyethylene bag, labeled 'Donation Bin – Sector G, 11/1987'. Provenance documentation incomplete; accession file references 'estate material from unknown source, transferred via regional sorting hub'.
descriptive_fields.historical_context: No contextual documentation available. Item not referenced in any known estate inventories or transfer manifests beyond internal sorting tag. No associated archival materials received with object. Storage history indicates object held in climate-controlled general storage since intake, with no prior conservation treatment or analytical testing.
descriptive_fields.notes: Initial triage assessment conducted by collections assistant on intake date. Object assigned temporary identifier and stored in non-buffered tissue within sealed archival container due to observed particulate shedding. Odor assessment: faint earthy scent noted at time of unpacking, not currently detectable. No biohazard indicators observed. X-radiography not performed. UV examination not conducted. Minimal handling protocol advised pending review. Cataloguing initiated using default template for unclassified materials. Field 'object_name' left as placeholder pending expert assessment.

condition.condition_notes: Surface particulate loss observed in handling; no active pest infestation. Core structure appears intact but fragile. No evidence of mold or moisture damage under current storage conditions. Long-term stability uncertain due to material heterogeneity and lack of identification. Recommended storage: inert enclosure, low-light, 45–55% RH, 18–20°C.

state.collection_link: Native American Ethnographic Materials Collection (1880–1945), Subseries C: Unaccessioned Field Notes and Artifacts
state.administrative_notes: Item transferred from temporary storage Room 12B during 2019 inventory audit. Initial receipt date unclear; penciled notation on crate tag reads 'Oct 1938?' but no matching accession log entry located. Crate labeled 'Dr. Elbridge H. Witherby – Northwest Survey – Misc. Indigenous Items'. Original packing materials (straw, burlap, wax paper) retained and stored separately under ID MA-PKG-1938-7742-STRW. No conservation treatment performed. Storage environment: 50% RH, 18°C, low-light archival room.
state.provenance: Reportedly collected during anthropological fieldwork in the Columbia Plateau region between 1936 and 1938. Collector’s field logs (unprocessed, uncataloged) reference 'donations from local residents' and 'surface finds near waterways'. Exact provenance obscured due to incomplete documentation. No tribal affiliation formally recorded at time of intake. Current institutional policy requires consultation before further description or public dissemination.
state.physical_description: Composite bundle wrapped in deteriorated cotton cloth, secured with faded red twine. Bundle measures approximately 22 cm x 14 cm x 9 cm. Surface soiling evident; minor insect damage along lower edge of cloth. Interior contains multiple undifferentiated organic materials: fragments of worked wood (approx. 3–5 cm in length), animal hair strands (brown and black), a partial avian claw, and several small stones. One stone fragment shows possible pigment residue (red ochre). No metal components detected during visual inspection. Object weight: 87 grams.
state.descriptive_notes: Bundle exhibits characteristics consistent with ceremonial or protective assemblages documented among some Plateau tribes. However, without contextual records or ethnographic verification, functional interpretation remains speculative. No inscriptions, maker’s marks, or identifying features observed. Odor of aged plant material faintly present upon opening. Re-wrapped using archival tissue and returned to sealed container immediately after examination to minimize exposure.
state.reproduction_status: No formal reproduction history. Photographic documentation not yet completed. Use of bundle contents for display, research, or reproduction prohibited pending tribal consultation and cultural sensitivity review.
state.condition: Stable but fragile. Textile wrapping shows signs of fiber weakening; handling restricted. Contents intact but not individually stabilized. Recommended storage: inert polyester sleeve within sealed archival box, away from light and fluctuating humidity. Pest monitoring tag in container shows no recent activity.

images.notes: High-resolution still taken under diffuse lighting with scale. Bundle unopened. Focus on exterior wrapping only.

state.workflow_remarks: Item flagged during routine backlog processing. Initial discipline assignment attempted as 'ethnography' but reassigned due to incomplete data and unresolved cultural affiliation. Further action contingent on image capture and external consultation.
state.final_note: Although the bundle has not been opened or analyzed beyond surface examination, tribal representatives previously consulted on related materials from the same collector have indicated that certain enclosed components may be considered spiritually sensitive. Public access to visual or descriptive data must be restricted until formal consultation is completed and permissions granted.

descriptive_fields.title: Ceramic Storage Vessel (Olla)
descriptive_fields.description: Globular ceramic olla with rounded base, short neck, and everted rim. Surface exhibits hand-smoothed finish with alternating burnished and matte bands. Despite initial field notes suggesting ceremonial use, contextual analysis indicates this vessel was likely used for everyday food storage rather than ritual purposes. Provenance traces to a domestic midden deposit in the Upper Gila region.

descriptive_fields.medium: Mahogany, brass fittings, ink residue, paper fragments
descriptive_fields.dimensions: Height: 92 cm, Width: 76 cm, Depth: 45 cm
descriptive_fields.provenance: Formerly believed to have belonged to William Wordsworth; re-examination confirms it was part of a later 19th-century collector’s assemblage. No direct link to the Wordsworth circle. Original attribution retracted in 2022 following archival review.
descriptive_fields.description: A Regency-era writing desk containing concealed compartments with fragmented manuscript drafts. descriptive.physical_description: Cylindrical organic bundle, partially unwrapped during initial inspection in 1988. Contained within a sealed archival polyethylene sleeve with silica gel desiccant. Accompanying documentation consists of three typewritten pages on onion-skin paper with handwritten annotations in brown ink, affixed with deteriorating pressure-sensitive tape. Reference made to 'specimen B-7' and 'the binding ritual of the eastern path,' with no further contextual elaboration.

state.title: Hand-drawn Topographical Survey of the Northern Parcels of the Old Crown Timber Reserve, District 7B
state.alternate_name: Timber Survey Map, Crown Reserve 7B - Northern Section
state.creator: Department of Lands and Forests, Provincial Survey Division
state.extent: 3 sheets: manuscript map; ink on linen; mounted on cloth backing
state.medium: Black ink and red annotation on linen, hand-colored in green wash for forested areas, with marginal notations in brown iron gall ink
state.support: Linen mounted on cotton duck backing with starch paste; joined with linen tape along vertical seams
state.notation: Surveyor’s annotations in margin: 'Elevation contours at 10-ft intervals; verified by triangulation from Benchmark #44 at Mill Creek Junction.'
state.provenance: Transferred from the Provincial Archives Depository, Regional Office #3, in 1976 as part of the Government Closure and Records Redistribution Act (1974). Originally held in the custody of the Ministry of Natural Resources, District 7 Field Office.
state.administrative_history: The Department of Lands and Forests was established in 1920 to oversee timber extraction, land use planning, and conservation efforts in rural districts. District 7B was active from 1915 to 1932, after which its territories were reassigned due to administrative consolidation.
state.scope_content: Three-sheet manuscript map detailing topography, tree density, soil composition, and proposed access routes in the northern sector of the Crown Timber Reserve. Includes hand-annotated notes on timber species (primarily white pine and red oak), drainage patterns, and survey control points. North arrow oriented to magnetic north as of 1928. Marginalia include survey team names (illegible in places), instrument calibration dates, and field corrections dated up to July 1928.
state.arrangement: Sheets arranged sequentially from west to east. Sheet 1 (westernmost), Sheet 2 (central), Sheet 3 (easternmost). Overlap between sheets is approximately 5 cm along vertical joins.
state.condition: Stable but fragile. Linen support exhibits moderate discoloration due to prolonged light exposure prior to archival storage. Minor ink flaking observed along fold lines of Sheet 2; red annotations slightly faded. Backing fabric shows no evidence of mold or insect activity. Adhesive used in mounting has stiffened over time, limiting flexibility. No active deterioration detected.
state.conservation_history: Conservation assessment conducted in 1989. Surface cleaned with soft brush; localized stabilization of ink edges using 2% isinglass solution. No deacidification performed. Rehoused in custom Solander box with inert foam spacers in 1991.
state.reproduction_note: No photographic reproductions were made during the initial archival intake. A digital scan was attempted in 2003 but abandoned due to size constraints of available equipment.
state.access_conditions: Open for research access with prior appointment. Gloves required for physical handling. Digital surrogate not available.
state.use_conditions: Permission required for publication. Credit line: 'Provincial Museum of Historical Geography, Collection of Government Survey Records.'
state.related_materials: See also: Series GOV-1920s-SURV, Subseries 7B-TIMBER, Files 12–18, which contain field notebooks, correspondence, and instrument logs related to this survey.
state.notes: Map was folded into eighths during storage for over 40 years; crease patterns remain visible despite flattening efforts. Ink remains legible throughout. No evidence of tracing or pounce transfer; appears to be original field draft. Not stamped with approval seal, suggesting it was a working copy rather than a final submission. However, all survey data aligns with official records in adjacent districts.
state.decision: Record finalized and approved for public release. All required metadata fields completed, verified against institutional standards, and internally reviewed.

administrative.provenance_notes: Collected during the joint Museum Victoria–University of Melbourne Expedition to Cape York Peninsula, 1933. Object retrieved during site survey near Mission River; exact site coordinates recorded in expedition field notebook #7 (archival reference MV-EXP-1933-CY-NB7), currently stored in the Restricted Research Archive. Collector reported oral accounts from two senior community members regarding use and cultural context; these recordings were transcribed in 1934 and remain under restricted access due to cultural protocols.

descriptive.form: Elongated, slightly curved shaft with distal hook and proximal hand grip. One lateral stabilizer fin present on upper surface near distal end. Surface wear consistent with use. Groove along dorsal midline extending from hook to midpoint. No evidence of hafted point attachment.
descriptive.decoration: Incised geometric patterning along midshaft; motif includes parallel zigzag lines and dot impressions. Pigment staining observed in incised areas, suggesting deliberate application. Pattern does not extend to distal hook or grip area.
descriptive.contextual_notes: Object was collected from surface context near a cleared area adjacent to a seasonal watercourse. Collector’s notes indicate it was found lying beneath a partially fallen eucalyptus tree. No associated objects were recovered in immediate vicinity. Local community representatives later indicated that such objects were traditionally discarded or left in place after ceremonial use under certain conditions, though this specific context was not confirmed.
descriptive.cultural_affiliation: Attributed to the Kaurareg people based on collector’s field notes and linguistic data from the expedition, though this designation has been subject to revision in later literature due to shifting understandings of territorial boundaries in the Torres Strait region during the early 20th century.

condition.condition_notes: Minor surface cracking along dorsal midline; no active deterioration observed. Fibre binding remnants are fragile and loosely attached. Resin residue is stable. Ochre traces are adhered but may be susceptible to abrasion. No signs of insect activity or fungal growth in recent inspections (last examined 2003-11-17). Recommended storage in low-light, climate-controlled environment with minimal handling. Conservation treatment in 1991 included controlled humidification and surface cleaning; report filed under MV-CONS-1991-044.

conservation_history.notes: No structural repairs performed. Fragments of fibre secured with reversible adhesive.

related_collections.collection_name: Oral History Recordings – Cape York Peninsula, 1934

access_restriction.reason: Cultural sensitivity regarding ceremonial use and symbolic motifs; consultation with descendant communities ongoing. High-resolution images and detailed contextual data not to be published without approval from relevant Traditional Owner groups. Physical access requires research application and cultural clearance.

descriptive_fields.object_name: Cast Iron Bench Grinder with Wooden Base
descriptive_fields.title: Double-Wheel Bench Grinder, manually operated, circa 1878
descriptive_fields.physical_description: The grinder features two opposing abrasive stone wheels mounted on a shared steel axle, driven via a cast iron foot pedal linkage system. The wooden base shows mortise-and-tenon joinery, with visible tool marks consistent with hand-planing. A manufacturer’s plaque, affixed to the rear upright support, reads: 'Hartwell & Sons, Birmingham, Reg. No. 18472'. Minor chipping present on the edge of the left grinding wheel. No evidence of motorized retrofitting. Pedal linkage operates with moderate resistance; lubrication points show residue of animal-fat-based grease. Base bears several indistinct hand-written numerals in white chalk, likely workshop identifiers.
descriptive_fields.provenance: Acquired in 1987 from the estate of Alfred T. Pembroke (deceased 1986), a retired mechanical engineer from Leeds. According to accompanying documentation, the object was used in Pembroke’s private workshop from approximately 1905 until 1948. Prior ownership chain unclear; no export records or customs documentation available. Donated under Accession Agreement NATMUS-ACQ-1987.0421. No known cultural restrictions apply.

exhibition_history.exhibition_title: Industry and Ingenuity: Tools of the Victorian Age
Machines We Made: Craft and Mechanization, 1800–1900

descriptive_fields.notes: Inventory check performed March 2023. Object remains in storage, Bay 7, Rack 14B. Environmental logs show stable humidity (48–52%) and temperature (19–21°C) since 2010. Conservation assessment scheduled Q2 2024. No pest activity observed in vicinity. Handling protocol: two-person lift, gloves required. Base slightly unlevel due to wood settling; does not affect structural integrity.

condition.conservation_history: Light surface cleaning performed in 1988. Axle realigned in 1991. No major restoration.
damage: Chipping on left grinding wheel (diameter ~1.2 cm)
Minor warping in wooden base (front edge, ~3 mm deflection)
Faint rust spotting on axle near right wheel (inactive)
condition.stability: Suitable for display with climate controls. Avoid prolonged direct sunlight.

state.title: Wooden Spearthrower, Mission River Area, West Cape York Peninsula
state.geographic_origin: Mission River Area, West Cape York Peninsula, Queensland, Australia
state.description: A hand-carved wooden spearthrower (woomera) collected during an anthropological survey in 1933. The tool features incised geometric patterning along the shaft and remnants of red ochre pigment. Functional wear marks are present at the grip and spur. Traditionally used to extend the velocity and range of light spears, this example reflects regional design characteristics of the Western Cape York Peninsula.

descriptive_fields.title: Fragmentary Ceramic Vessel (Upper Body and Rim)
descriptive_fields.alternate_name: Storage jar sherd, Late Iron Age
descriptive_fields.description: Recovered from excavation unit F7 at the Blackthorn Hill site. The fragment includes part of the everted rim and upper body, with traces of carbonized residue on the interior, suggesting use in food storage or cooking. Surface treatment shows coarse hand-coiling and partial burnishing. Notched decoration near the rim indicates regional stylistic traits common in southern British late pre-Roman contexts. Initially thought to be from a domestic hearth context, further stratigraphic review confirms it was lifted from a ritual pit deposit—retracting earlier field notes that classified it as domestic refuse.
descriptive_fields.provenance: Excavated 1987, Blackthorn Hill, Oxfordshire, UK. Associated with pit feature 12, context 3.

state.reproduction_status: No reproduction allowed pending rights review
state.condition: Stable, fragmented; minor surface abrasion, no active deterioration
related_collection_links: Oxford Archaeological Unit – Blackthorn Hill Archive (Collection BH-1987)
British Museum – Late Iron Age Pottery Database (Ref: BM-LIA-202)

state.title: Field Notebook and Pencil Recovered from the 1926 Arctic Expedition Site
state.creator: Unknown (attributed to expedition member)
state.physical_description: Leather-bound notebook (12 x 8 cm), partially water-damaged, containing handwritten notes in pencil; accompanied by a broken graphite pencil with manufacturer stamp 'H&H 1924'.

state.descriptive_notes: Entries appear to document daily weather observations and supply inventories. One page contains a sketch of a coastal formation matching the Banks Island region. Indigenous oral history from the Inuvialuit community suggests the site may be associated with a spiritual event involving a lost traveler; this connection remains unverified but is under review by the museum's Indigenous Liaison Committee.

state.condition: fragile; ink bleeding, cover detaching, requires conservation stabilization

state.object_name: International Mercator Projection Navigational Chart, Atlantic Ocean Sector

creator.corporate_body: Hydrographic Office of the British Admiralty

physical_description.support: Two-part articulated backing with cotton interleaf
physical_description.color_palette: Sepia-tone ink with cobalt blue hydrographic notations, black contour lines, and ochre marginal annotations
physical_description.marginalia: Handwritten annotations in faded graphite along lower right border; includes partial coordinates and tide notation 'Spring High Water, 1893 Mar 18'.

provenance.source: Transferred from the Royal Naval College, Dartmouth, via inter-institutional deaccession agreement dated 1978-09-15

current_location.repository: National Maritime Archives and Collections Division

environmental_conditions.storage_orientation: Horizontal, flat storage in acid-free portfolio

state.descriptive_notes: This chart forms part of the late 19th-century standardization of international maritime navigation systems. It employs a modified Mercator projection with incremental magnetic declination indicators calibrated for annual variation in 1893. The map covers latitudinal range 15°N to 50°N and longitudinal extent 80°W to 20°W, focusing on transatlantic shipping lanes between North America and Western Europe. Topographic detail is limited to coastal elevations; bathymetric data is rendered in fathom contours at 10-fathom intervals. Compass roses are positioned at 1,200-mile intervals. The cartouche includes a warning in English and French regarding 'magnetic anomalies in the vicinity of the Sargasso Sea'. Registration marks for printing alignment are visible at all four corners. Minor insect damage observed along left margin, non-impairing. No evidence of field use, such as folding wear or ink stains from logs.

condition.preservation_status: Treated for mold resistance in 1985; no active deterioration
damage: Minor delamination (approx. 2cm) at upper left seam between sheets
Faint water stain in lower right quadrant, not affecting legibility

conservation_history.procedure: Reinforcement of sheet junction with Japanese tissue overlay

reproduction.reproduction_method: Lithographic duplication from master copper plate

images.description: Full-spread digital capture under controlled raking light; shows surface texture and ink saturation.

related_collections.relationship: Original production records and master plates

related_collections.institution: Maritime History Collection, Library of Congress
related_collections.relationship: Supplementary logbooks and route annotations from vessels using similar charts

cataloguer.name: Dr. E. M. Thorne
cataloguer.verification_status: Cross-referenced with Admiralty production logs and transfer documentation

The source system is currently on the corporate allowlist, and the account credentials were last rotated 72 hours prior to the event.
